process: Online MCQs covering DSA, OOP, databases, OS, and general aptitude, followed by a coding round - fresh-grad hiring has included a long onsite coding test.
topics: OOP - all four pillars (encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction)
Your Final Year Project - be ready to explain it in real depth
note: Leans more technical than behavioral - solid DSA/OOP fundamentals matter more here than soft skills.

process: A technical assessment, then an HR call, then a roughly 90-minute technical interview with the project manager.
topics: Every tool/technology listed on your resume - expect "how, why, and when did you use this"
note: Expect to be quizzed in detail on anything you've listed on your resume - don't list a tool you can't discuss confidently.

process: A multi-round process (roughly 3 weeks): initial screening, technical assessments, multiple panel discussions, and a final onsite round.
topics: Data structures - e.g. array vs. linked list
Describing a challenging bug you fixed
note: Problem-solving and communication questions ("how do you learn a new technology quickly") come up alongside the technical rounds, not just after them.

process: An online assessment (OOP, SQL, JavaScript, HTML/CSS), then a technical interview with the local manager, an HR round, and a final interview with an offshore manager - notably one of the longer processes, often 5-6 rounds.
topics: OOP MCQs - inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation, overriding
SQL/DBMS - normalization, index types, writing functional queries
Angular and SQL Server (for relevant tracks)
note: One of the longer hiring processes among Pakistani software houses - budget time for multiple rounds.

process: An HR call, a first technical interview, a second technical interview with an architect focused on system design, a conversation with a director on leadership/collaboration, and a final alignment/compensation call.
note: A more senior-leaning process with a dedicated system-design round - a stronger fit for candidates past entry level.

process: An HR resume screen, an online test (MCQs or a coding assessment depending on the track), two back-to-back technical interviews, a management/VP round, and often a final round billed as "HR" that several candidates report turned out to still be technical. Most reports put the whole process at 1-2 weeks.
topics: OOP concepts and common design patterns
SQL - writing queries across multiple tables
Stack-specific questions matching the role (e.g. Android-specific questions for mobile roles)
note: Don't let your guard down on the "final HR round" - multiple candidates report it turned out to still include technical questions.

process: A recruiter screen, an online coding test, and then several back-to-back technical interviews with the engineering team, followed by a hiring-manager round.
topics: System design basics (e.g. designing a simplified dispatch or tracking system)
Core CS fundamentals behind your resume's stack
note: Pakistan-specific reports are limited, but the loop mirrors Careem's standard process at its other regional offices - expect genuine coding and system-design rounds, not just behavioral screening.

process: An online application, an HR call, and an online technical interview with a QA engineer.
topics: Manual testing fundamentals - SDLC, regression testing, bug lifecycle
Writing a test case for a given flow
Basic SQL (e.g. second-highest value from a table)
note: Available reports specifically cover the SQA/QA track, not general software engineering roles - most useful if you're applying to that track.
